3
The units of specific heat capacity are J kg–1
K–1.
What are the SI base units of specific heat capacity?
K–1
B
m s–1
K–1
C
m2
s–2
K–1
D
m2
s–1
A
m s–2
K–1

hints: Start with the given $\text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$ and notice that $\text{J}$ is not an SI base unit so it must be expanded.
Recall energy from work as $W = Fs$, so $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$ and force as $F = ma$, so $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Substitute the $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ form of the joule into the $\text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$ expression and cancel $\text{kg}$ once.
walkthrough: Identify the given unit: specific heat capacity is $\text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$, where $\text{K}$ is already a base unit but $\text{J}$ and $\text{kg}^{-1}$ need attention.
State the rule for the joule: from $W = Fs$, $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$, and from $F = ma$, $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Combine them: $1 \text{ J} = (1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2})(1 \text{ m}) = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}$.
Substitute into specific heat capacity: $\text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} = (\text{kg m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2}) \times \text{kg}^{-1} \times \text{K}^{-1}$.
Cancel one $\text{kg}$ with $\text{kg}^{-1}$ to give $\text{m}^2 \text{ s}^{-2} \text{ K}^{-1}$, which checks as energy per mass per temperature. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is $\text{m s}^{-2} \text{K}^{-1}$, the unit of acceleration per kelvin, with only one power of $\text{m}$ instead of $\text{m}^2$.

B.explanation: This is $\text{m s}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$, the unit of velocity per kelvin, with wrong powers of both $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.

C.explanation: Expanding $\text{J}$ to $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$ and dividing by $\text{kg K}$ leaves $\text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-2} \text{K}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: This has $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-2}$, so it does not match the $\text{s}^{-2}$ from expanding the joule.
